complexity.review_note: Preserve all but one upvoted candidate after four natural reassignments. Retain major class separations, uniform/nonuniform circuits, formula composition, reachability, total search, minimum circuit size and PCPs. The closely related conditional MCSP consequence is the explicit upvote exception.

automata.review_note: Balance finite and two-way automata, grammar equivalence, tree automata and transformations, quantitative automata, timed/register/infinite-word models, pattern avoidance and cellular dynamics. Omit narrow variants of grammar universality, limit sets and periodicity in favor of model diversity; retain one upvoted reset-threshold landmark.

computability.review_note: Keep two broad degree-structure questions rather than the many c.e./enumeration-degree variants. Cover machine universality, randomness, algorithmic information, computable real geometry, reverse mathematics and matrix-semigroup decidability. Two upvoted imports add digit-generation and reversible computation.

proof.review_note: Select Extended Frege as the main unrestricted lower-bound target and retain the upvoted Frege/Extended Frege simulation question. Broaden to proof search, optimal proof systems, modular and XOR systems, arithmetic strength, algebraic/geometric simulation, and proof time-space tradeoffs. The ordinary Frege lower bound and several nearby space variants remain red.

communication.review_note: Cover deterministic rank, quantum/classical models, Fourier analysis, compression, threshold-function influence, evasiveness, direct sums and multiparty communication. Omit nearby rank/partition and Fourier min-entropy variants rather than occupying most places with them.

fine.review_note: Keep every upvoted fine-grained candidate after moving real-weight APSP to Algorithms. Distinguish randomized integer APSP from the real comparison-addition model; include clique and gap-ETH to broaden the canonical hypothesis landscape. Randomized/nondeterministic SETH and weight-clique variants remain red.

randomness.review_note: Keep the two upvoted class equalities, then cover space-bounded PRGs, deterministic restricted-isometry matrices, interactive randomness, expansion, independent and seeded extraction, pseudodeterministic constructions and hitting-set/PRG conversion. P versus RP is a narrower class-equality neighbor of the retained P versus BPP target. Restricted-isometry construction moves to Algorithms; retain a second, structurally different circuit-generator model (AC0 with parity) here.

parameterized.review_note: Retain the main FPT/W[1] and ETH/set-cover barriers, kernelization both general and concrete, directed feedback, two distinct graph-width representations, formula SAT and the restored post-cutoff approximation-hardness result. Move weighted TSP and exact Subset Sum to Algorithms; move exact linear-extension counting to Counting. Avoid many variants of kernelization and width computation.

approximation.review_note: Keep the two upvoted landmarks, major hardness hypotheses and representative network-design, cut, cover, tour, feedback and clustering objectives. Use the overall metric-TSP approximation target instead of also selecting several TSP integrality-gap/ATSP variants.

online.review_note: Cover secretary/prophet models, geometric chasing, two scheduling models, bandit optimization, packing and calibration. Keep both deterministic and randomized k-server as distinct central targets, including the downvoted deterministic card. Use additive-one bin packing as the representative rather than keeping both it and constant-additive error.

beyond.review_note: All upvoted cards retained. Balance worst-to-average hardness, planted models, random constraint refutation, smoothed local search, random assignment/tours and concrete random-order/sorting analyses. Avoid selecting only statistical-inference thresholds or hardness-amplification variants.

sampling.review_note: Retain representative coloring, degree-sequence, spin-system, hard-core and self-avoiding-walk models alongside cutoff, cover time, matroid sampling and exact spanning-tree sampling. Reduce the cluster of Ising/Swendsen-Wang boundary-condition and exponent variants.

counting.review_note: Balance counting complexity, randomized and deterministic approximation, set-system/polytope enumeration, enumeration dichotomies and Gray codes. Include the post-cutoff exact linear-extension algorithm rather than only approximate graph counting. The conditional P=NP implication is omitted beside the primary FP/#P target.

structural.review_note: Cover expansion, minors, Ramsey/chi-boundedness, flows, extremal girth, excluded grids, reconstruction, list edge coloring and directed cycles. Retain only one girth card and one reconstruction card. Replace another chromatic-number inequality with excluded-grid structure. The upvoted Ramanujan existence question stays green.

graph-algorithms.review_note: Keep all six upvoted cards, then exact matching, triangle detection, negative-weight shortest paths and cut compression. General Exact Matching is green; bipartite TCS-0611 is red as explicitly requested. Avoid filling the remaining places with more flow/connectivity variants or a second Ramanujan construction target.

data-structures.review_note: Dynamic optimality represents the BST-conjecture cluster. Cover static and dynamic lower bounds, dictionaries, indexing, succinct rank/select, online labels, heaps, external memory and retroactivity. Include the restored rank/select result. Select the dynamic dictionary rather than both static and dynamic dictionary variants.

dynamic.review_note: Retain principal connectivity, matching, distance, forest and cut targets; broaden to directed ordering, logical expressiveness, planarity, string distances and planar geometry. Omit nearby connectivity, graph-width and coloring variants, rather than making the entire category about graph connectivity.

strings.review_note: All upvoted cards are green. The two edit-distance approximations have different requirements: a constant factor in n polylog n versus 1+epsilon in n^(1+o(1)); do not falsely assert an implication. Retain trace reconstruction, grammar compression, multiple alignment, LCS, Hamming matching, tree edits and BWT-run indexing. Move metric embedding to Geometry; omit the weaker subquadratic 1+epsilon variant.

game.review_note: Represent fair division, welfare, truthful auctions/scheduling, black-box mechanism conversion, cake cutting, equilibrium inefficiency, game equilibria and social choice. Keep the main complete-EFX existence target instead of its numerous approximation/agent-count variants, and use one auction model rather than several closely related welfare mechanisms.

algebra.review_note: Retain matrix/integer arithmetic, PIT, field factorization, a monoid word problem, radical comparison, group isomorphism, tensor decomposition, tropical feasibility and addition chains. Select one representative of the several one-relator group/monoid decision problems and omit restricted PIT variants. The restored tensor-decomposition result stays eligible and green. Min-plus feasibility is red because the cited source proves equivalence to retained mean-payoff games TCS-6568; exact Kronecker-polytope membership adds a different algebraic representation question.

algebraic-complexity.review_note: Combine VP/VNP and permanent/determinant landmarks with formulas, real-arithmetic classes, integer-root bounds, rank and asymptotic tensor rank, rigidity, characteristic-dependent factor closure and noncommutative circuits. Omit multiple adjacent branching-program/formula and multilinearity variants; the upvoted real-machine separation is moved here.

lattices.review_note: Balance Diophantine decidability, factoring, discrete logarithms, nonresidues and prime construction against approximation, quantum algorithms, deterministic hardness, exact space-efficient lattice search and structured ring-LWE reductions. Limit the many close SVP hardness/gap/reduction variants; include the restored deterministic-hardness result.

coding.review_note: Cover packing, two multiuser channel families, network coding, local decoding, entropy decision questions, computability of capacity, interactive tree codes, deletions and distributed lossy compression. Avoid filling the category with several interference-channel and rate/distance variants. Move the explicit capacity-achieving decoding algorithm to Algorithms.

testing.review_note: Represent structural classification and removal bounds, testing versus estimation, density learning and instance-optimal distribution testing, submodularity/monotonicity, local graph reconstruction, convexity and matrix rank. Omit single-pattern cases and several graph-access variants. General density learning moves to Learning; Markov-chain identity testing adds dependent-observation distribution testing.

csp.review_note: Retain finite promise and infinite-domain dichotomies, one general approximate-coloring target, search versus decision, restricted CSP, Holant, representation power, valued constraints, non-redundancy and meta-tractability. Omit adjacent 3-coloring thresholds and narrow search variants.

database.review_note: Keep the upvoted ontology-entailment card, but balance it with multiset containment, enumeration, key repairs, deletion resilience, join-size bounds, finite controllability, recursive semiring evaluation, probabilistic reliability and parallel join processing. The restored linear-rule/transitivity question remains a red alternative to avoid overconcentrating on entailment.

misc.review_note: Ten distinct themes: sunflowers, partial orders, union closure, orthogonal designs, matroid bases, zero-error graph capacity, additive-combinatorial growth, small-deviation probability, symbolic dynamics and simultaneous Diophantine separation. Subset-sum extremal encoding and Langton ant remain red alternatives. The two 2026 solution claims are retained with their scientific caveats.

ads.review_note: Strengthen the initially sparse general category with real-weight APSP, exact TSP/Subset Sum, efficient decoding, Steiner approximation and explicit restricted-isometry construction. Cover sorting, sparsification, representations, optimization and graph-path/detection problems. Omit nearby spanner and isomorphism-classification variants and the lowest-priority tail.

semantics.review_note: Balance arithmetic decision problems, recurrence zeros/signs, games, finite-model and descriptive complexity, type theory, lambda semantics, unification/rewriting, probabilistic denotational semantics, counter systems, concurrent algebra, SAT proof search and logical definability. Reduce recurrence, word-equation, HoTT and finite-model variants rather than selecting the first 25 mechanically. Mean-payoff games represents the equivalent min-plus feasibility card TCS-0046.

parallel.review_note: All six upvoted cards retained, including the original Euclidean MST streaming proposal. Cover circuit parallelism, parallel work efficiency, LOCAL/CONGEST/MPC, quantum locality, sketching and streaming, mergeability and asynchronous shared-memory/agreement. Keep one FIFO/Common2 formulation. The two restored agreement results remain green; omit repeated graph distance/coloring/model variants.

optimization.review_note: Balance continuous/discrete algorithms, discrepancy, numerical matrix analysis, polyhedral structure, memory/query complexity, volume, manifold optimization, submodularity, low-rank approximation, sequential exploration, fixed points and local minimax optimization. Keep Komlos rather than also the Beck-Fiala special case, and general sparse systems rather than another Laplacian log-factor target. Import CLS and submodular maximization to broaden computational optimization.

geometry.review_note: Cover convex geometry, metric embeddings, extremal incidence/range questions, geometric algorithms, unfolding, drawings, flips and several distinct low-dimensional topology targets. Keep the post-cutoff EMD-distortion result and import edit-distance distortion. Omit repeated EMD streaming/sketching and three-manifold certificate variants; include output-sensitive hulls, visibility and instance-optimal polytope approximation.

learning.review_note: Retain flagship representation-learning and sample-compression questions, but reduce close halfspace, compression and decision-tree variants. Cover computational hardness, noisy learning, Gaussian estimation, online/multiclass rates, conditional information, membership/SQ models, teaching, reinforcement learning, robust estimation and dependent observations. Imports add a perceptron threshold and general Gaussian-mixture density learning.

crypto.review_note: All upvoted cards retained. Balance core existence and assumption reductions with sharing, verification, encryption, hashing, zero knowledge, number-theoretic foundations, quantum money, retrieval, non-malleability and secure computation. Four privacy representatives cover statistical learning, release, continual observation and decision-making. Avoid taking every closely related LWE-based encryption variant or every strengthening of the same one-way-function assumption.

quantum.review_note: All fourteen upvoted cards retained. Add condensed-matter structure, entanglement, error correction, memory, channel capacity, entropy, nonlocal games, query gaps, sampling and synthesis. Do not fill the remainder with further QMA/PCP variants. The strong total-function communication separation TCS-4952 is red because the broader relation question is retained as TCS-6450, independently of its downvote.

moves.reason: Real-arithmetic machine classes are a natural part of algebraic complexity; preserves an upvoted problem while broadening that small category.
Digit-generation complexity and the nature of computable real numbers fit this small category and broaden its coverage.
Universal reversible machine simulation connects computational models and their resource requirements.
The continuous-local-search complexity class belongs naturally with the computational foundations of optimization.

The general real-weight APSP algorithm is a natural Algorithms landmark. Moving it strengthens that comparatively sparse large category, while Fine-grained complexity retains the distinct integer hypothesis and an APSP-to-3SUM reduction.
A flagship exact traveling-salesperson algorithm strengthens the broad Algorithms selection; specialized parameterized cards remain in the small category.
The canonical exact Subset Sum running-time barrier complements the large category, with a distinct parameter regime from pseudopolynomial/output-sensitive Subset Sum.
This restored exact counting question is most naturally reviewed alongside other counting algorithms rather than graph-parameterized problems.
The distortion of edit distance into l1 is a metric-embedding question. This natural large-category home preserves the problem while opening a string-algorithm place for another model.

Explicit construction with efficient capacity-achieving list decoding is a central coding algorithm. It adds a computational domain to the broad Algorithms category while Coding retains its core information-theoretic and local/interactive-code questions.
The central Steiner-tree approximation problem strengthens the general algorithmic selection while the small approximation category retains ten other broad representatives.

Explicit restricted-isometry matrix construction adds a major algorithmic domain to the comparatively sparse general category; Pseudorandomness retains representative PRGs, extraction, expansion and class equalities.
Value-oracle submodular maximization under a matroid is a natural optimization target and complements the retained minimization/query questions.
The random perceptron threshold belongs naturally with computational learning and statistical inference; improves breadth relative to further compression variants.
Efficient density learning is a core learning problem. Property testing retains distinct distribution testing and estimation targets.

upvoted_red.TCS-6168: Retain the central Minimum Circuit Size Problem (TCS-4786) and the direct circuit-complexity question for EXP (TCS-0020). This card asks for a conditional implication between their two themes; omit it to leave room for probabilistically checkable proofs (TCS-7268). This is a diversity choice, not a claim that either retained problem implies it.
